If you hit thrifts, worth checking the water bottle & travel mug area. Many times you'll see $1-2 range containers that were over $20 new. Some like the dual-wall vacuum Kleen Kanteen, Nissan, & Sendestar ones in the $30-50 range. Have picked up several still tagged and were likely gifts. I used to be a Sigg loyalist but migrated onto other brands as they offer advantages. If you only run your cooking area once in the morning and not again until evening (we do this during blackouts), dual-wall vacuum units are great for keeping coffee, water, soup/stew hot all day. (This is no different than wide-mouth Thermos or Aladdin vacuum bottles but those always seem to be priced higher at thrifts.) Finally, the majority of these all fit standard bike bottle cages. There are also ones much bigger too.

Some thoughts -

Kleen Kanteen

Unpainted raw finish stainless ones can be found in both single-wall and dual-wall vacuum models. They share the same stopper threading and there are 2 types of stoppers from reinforced plastic. One is a screw down while the other has a mouthpiece like a bike bottle. The mouth on them is wide enough to allow ice cubes put in or a fishmouth hanger to be used. If you don't carry a pot but want to heat liquid, a stainless single-wall Kleen Kanteen w/ fishmouth hanger lets you put it over a fire. The dual-wall vacuum ones will keep liquid warm as good as a regular Thermos-type vacuum bottle. Obviously you cannot put a dual-wall over a fire and get the contents hot.

Nissan

Quality brand, well made & rugged. They will take a good drop and keep the lid on. You will usually find these in with the travel mugs and they are dual-wall vacuum, wide-mouth types. They aren't travel mugs though, more like a jar. (Their regular vacuum bottles are good to.)

Sendestar

Have not seen anything other than dual-wall, wide mouth & painted ones of various capacity. Mouth big enough to allow something thick like stew to go in. Hot items remain near temp they went in for whole day. Overall good quality and rugged build.

Sigg

All made in Switzerland and high-quality, I hiked for years with nothing but these. However, they have not aged well. First, they are aluminum. Over time they corrode at the threads and even inside.I've only found single-wall types (not sure if they make a dual-wall vacuum one). They now make a wide mouth unit but I've never found one nor am I going to spend ~$40 to try it out. The regular style mouth is quite small so low viscosity liquids only. Tough to hang over a fire with a fishmouth hanger and not sure I'd want to do that with an aluminum bottle anyway. Stopper size is proprietary to Sigg so if you lose one, there is no equivalent. I've retired most of mine to fuel bottle use.

Thermos

A brand as old as the hills but still good. These will all be dual-wall vacuum like the Nissan ones and in similar configuration. You will also find plenty of Thermos travels mugs (Aladdin too) and for mugs, they seem to keep liquids the hottest.

Many other brands out there such as Aura, Stanley, etc. but the above are the ones I have direct experience on. For single-wall stainless there are plenty of generic Chinese ones that are just as well built as the branded ones. I wouldn't pass one over for that, just look at how it is made. When I hike I've settled on single-wall Kleen Kanteens as my go to with a Nissan dual-wall wide mouth to carry hot food. For home use we have a Sendestar 64 oz. and it keeps coffee hot all day. My travel mug used to be a Thermos made unit but I dropped it. Broke the handle off and tore the bracket spot-welded in the side which ended the vacuum. On the hunt for a replacement now. Hope the above is useful info.
